# Configure cycle detection

Deploy the Agentic Analytics component and connect it to Consul Agentic Runtime
Fabric to contain AI agents stuck in tool-call loops. When you finish, a
repeated tool call with unchanged results opens the agent's circuit, and Consul
rejects that agent's later requests.

@include '../../../global/partials/alerts/beta.mdx'

To learn how detection works, refer to [Cycle detection](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/cycle-detection).

## Requirements

- Consul Enterprise with a valid license for external processing, and the
  `consul-ai` [feature gate](/consul/docs/manage/feature-gates) enabled.
- A Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric deployment with agent services, Envoy data
  plane proxies, and the required external processors.
- The AI Inference Gateway and MCP sidecar on the model and tool paths your
  application uses, plus the identity and credential integrations it needs.
- [Auto-instrumentation](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/auto-instrumentation/configure-auto-instrumentation)
  configured, with trace context propagation, an OpenTelemetry collection path,
  and a trace backend that your analytics release supports.
- A BullMQ-compatible Redis or Valkey deployment for the analysis queue.
- A protection-state store.
- IBM Container Registry (ICR) access to the `csl-ag-ana`, `csl-ig-pro`, and
  `csl-nod-rly` images, and versions of the other Agentic Runtime Fabric
  components that are compatible with your analytics release.
- A behavior policy that defines agent scope, detection thresholds, circuit
  validity, recovery, and dependency-failure handling.

## Pull the Agentic Analytics images

Agentic Analytics needs three images: `csl-ag-ana` and its dependencies
`csl-ig-pro` and `csl-nod-rly`. You also need the images for Consul, the data
plane, and the other components in your deployment.

The images are in the IBM Container Registry. Replace `<registry>` with the
registry path supplied for your distribution and `<version>` with the analytics
release tag.

For Docker, run:

```shell-session
$ docker pull <registry>/csl-ag-ana:<version>
$ docker pull <registry>/csl-ig-pro:latest
$ docker pull <registry>/csl-nod-rly:latest
```

For Podman, run:

```shell-session
$ podman pull <registry>/csl-ag-ana:<version>
$ podman pull <registry>/csl-ig-pro:latest
$ podman pull <registry>/csl-nod-rly:latest
```

Authenticate to the registry with your container runtime's credential mechanism
when required. The dependency commands use the `latest` tag. For reproducible
deployments, pin approved release tags or digests in your deployment manifest.
Do not assume that an unqualified image name resolves to the intended registry.

Pulling the images does not connect them. The following sections configure the
trace, analysis, and enforcement paths.

## Connect traces to the analysis queue

<!-- TODO: Ask engineering to define "inference-path producer" in step 4, and when to use one instead of the span relay. No content defines what an inference-path producer is. -->

1. Extend trace context propagation to delegation calls between agents.
1. Include a stable, trusted agent identity in the trace that enforcement can
   also resolve.
1. Retrieve a workflow's spans by trace ID to confirm that storage works.
1. Configure the trace producer to queue trace IDs as evidence arrives. The
   local integration uses a span relay. An inference-path producer must also
   trigger analysis for later workflow activity.
1. Set the same queue backend, queue name, and prefix on the producer and the
   Agentic Analytics consumer. A mismatch leaves both services running with no
   analysis work delivered.
1. Configure the analytics worker's trace-query endpoint and credentials.
1. Confirm that the worker reaches the trace backend from its own network, not
   only from your machine.

Configure the queue backend for reliable delivery:

- Use the `noeviction` memory policy on the BullMQ backend, so queue data is not
  evicted.
- Configure persistence and capacity for your delivery guarantees. An in-memory
  development queue loses pending analysis triggers on restart.

The detector needs tool identity and comparable argument and output values in
the correlated workflow evidence. Use only representations that the analytics
component supports and your data-handling policy approves. Do not enable
unrestricted capture of prompts, arguments, results, credentials, or personal
data to feed the detector. Missing or redacted evidence can prevent the argument
comparison or limit findings.

## Configure analytics and circuit enforcement

Use the configuration schema and deployment manifest supplied with your
`csl-ag-ana` release. The following table lists the inputs to configure. The
names describe each input and are not literal configuration keys.

| Input | What to configure |
| --- | --- |
| Analytics image | The fully qualified `csl-ag-ana` image you pulled. |
| Dependency images | The `csl-ig-pro` and `csl-nod-rly` images, or approved pinned versions, in their deployment services. |
| Queue connection | Backend endpoint, authentication, queue name, and prefix shared with the producer. |
| Trace source | The trace backend's query endpoint and access credentials. |
| Cycle detector | Enable cycle analysis, and set the minimum repetition count and semantic similarity threshold. |
| Analysis scheduling | Bound concurrent traces and indexing waits, and keep passes for each trace serial. |
| Agent attribution | Map findings and requests to the same trusted agent identity and policy scope. |
| Circuit policy | When a finding opens a circuit, the reason recorded, and the validity and recovery rules. |
| Protection-state connection | Write access for the decision publisher and read access for enforcement processors. |
| Dependency failures | Handling for unavailable queues, missing traces, stale state, and failed state reads or writes. |

Start and connect the components:

1. Connect the analytics decision path to protection-state publication.
1. Configure the agent enforcement processors to read protection state before
   they forward requests.
1. Start the queue and state services, the trace backend, and the collection
   path.
1. Deploy the analytics service with the configured image, network access, and
   credentials.
1. Start the trace producer.
1. Confirm that the cycle detector is enabled and consuming the expected queue.

Detection logs alone do not show that Consul can open or enforce a circuit. Keep
storage and analytics endpoints private, and grant each component only the
access it needs.

## Verify detection and enforcement

Use a non-production agent workflow, and a test model or a bounded usage budget.

1. Run any workflow. Confirm that the trace producer queues its trace ID and
   that an Agentic Analytics worker consumes it. If no analysis runs, check this
   handoff first.
1. Run a workflow that calls the same tool with different arguments, such as
   successive `page` values, and receives new results. Confirm that the trace is
   analyzed and produces no finding.
1. Run a workflow that calls a tool with unchanged arguments and receives
   changing results. Confirm that it produces no finding.
1. Run a workflow in which one agent repeatedly calls `query_records` with
   `{"filter":"status:active","page":1}` and receives unchanged results. Exceed
   the repetition threshold. If the workflow summarizes between calls, keep the
   summaries unchanged too.
1. Confirm a finding for that trace and agent.
1. Confirm that behavior policy publishes an open circuit for the agent, with a
   reason and a validity period.
1. Send another request from the agent through the protected route. Confirm an
   HTTP `503` response, and confirm that the request does not reach the
   upstream.
1. Send a request from an unaffected agent to the same backend. Confirm that it
   succeeds.
1. Run the expiry or reset procedure. Confirm that Consul admits the agent's
   requests again.
1. Make analytics or protection-state storage unavailable. Confirm that the
   behavior matches your dependency-failure policy.

Inspect worker activity as well as queue state. An empty queue does not mean
that every scheduled pass finished, and a finding does not mean that enforcement
consumed the new state.
